blocks.text: Welcome to Canva AI

Canva is one of the most accessible tools for creating visual content. And with AI built directly in, going from idea to finished design is significantly faster, no design background required.

In this guide, you'll learn how to unlock Canva AI's full potential, from personal projects to professional work. Because with AI, you're no longer limited to static designs — you can generate text, video, and even code, all from a single prompt.
What Is Canva AI?
Canva AI is a prompt-driven creative tool built directly into Canva. Type an idea, upload a reference image, or speak a request — and it generates a finished, editable design.

Canva AI works across text, images, code, presentations, and video, and it's all in one place. 

Here's what the interface looks like.
The Interface

The Canva AI interface has three main areas: a central prompt field at the top, output tabs for switching between Design, Image, Doc, Code, and Video modes, and a sidebar on the left for creating, accessing, and re-editing previous generations.
Here's what each tab does:

• Design generates full layouts.
  • Image produces standalone visuals.
  • Doc drafts ready-to-use text content.
  • Code builds interactive elements.
  • Video creates motion clips.
The prompt field stays the same across all of them — the tab you select determines what comes out.
Let's start with a simple image generation. Select the Image tab, choose a style and an aspect ratio, and generate: a man climbing Mount Everest.

The Design Feature

You might already know Canva for presentations and social posts. This lesson is about what happens when you stop picking templates and start describing what you need instead: a wedding invitation, and a YouTube banner and letting Canva AI build it. 

You'll also learn how to keep every design on-brand and convert one format into another without starting over.

blocks.question: What can you use the Design tab for?

blocks.text: Generate a Design From a Prompt

The Design tab covers a wide range of creative needs — Social Media, Presentations, Marketing, Cards & Invitations, Logos, and more. Choose the right type and format for you, and it returns several complete, editable layouts to choose from.

Imagine you need to create a wedding invitation, but you don't want to look for a specific template in Canva. Choose the Design tab, pick Cards & Invitations, then select the Invitationformat and see what comes back. Let's try it.

blocks.prompt: Complete the prompt below to generate a personal design in the Design tab.

blocks.text: Refine With a Reference Image

Now you've realized the mood you set for the invitation isn't quite right — you want something more creative, but still want to keep that romantic feel. 

To get there, upload a reference image, and Canva AI will reflect your style much more closely. Let's use this wedding invitation as a reference.

blocks.prompt: Upload the reference image and refine your wedding invitation prompt.
blocks.template: [Command] a wedding invitation that looks like this *uploaded image*

blocks.text: You've got your invitations sorted, but what if you notice a mistake in the name or address? You can easily fix it manually in the Canva Editor.

So that's what the Design tab can do — it gives you several ready-made outputs to choose from, and if anything's slightly off, like a name, an address, or a color, you can fix it directly in the Canva Editor. The final touches are always yours to make.

The Design tab works just as well for other personal content. Take a YouTube banner for a Tokyo travel vlog. Head to the Design tab, pick the Social Media type, and choose the YouTube Banner format. Let's generate it.

blocks.prompt: Use the same Design tab to generate a YouTube banner for a travel vlog.

blocks.text: Canva AI returned a colorful result, but what if the colors or fonts don't quite match your personal style? That's where Brand Kit can help.

To generate a fully branded post, Canva AI will prompt you to set up a Brand Kit — a paid feature available on the Pro plan. This is where you customize your logo, colors, and fonts, keeping everything visually consistent across all your designs.

blocks.prompt: Update your YouTube banner using your Brand Kit colors.

blocks.text: The colors are locked in, now make sure the typography matches too. Choose a font for your headings, subheadings, section headers, body text, and quotes, and customize the size and style of each.
Excellent!

From there, every asset will automatically reflect your brand.

The next step is to create a single design that works across multiple formats.
Remix The Formats

Remix is built into how you prompt the Design tab. Describe what you want to convert, and Canva AI suggests new looks and structures automatically. Open an existing design, use "remix" in the prompt, and Canva will adapt the layout, colors, and format while keeping the content intact.

blocks.prompt: Take an existing design and convert it into a different format.

feedbackCorrect.text: Remix is right here. The content already exists — Remix restructures it into the new format automatically, so nothing needs to be rebuilt or rewritten.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Starting from scratch means recreating content that's already done. Remix carries everything across and adapts the structure, which is usually faster than rebuilding from a blank canvas.

Video and Motion Generation

Most people assume professional video content requires a full production pipeline, but with Canva AI's Video tab, the whole production process gets easier.

In this lesson, you'll use it to animate designs, add voiceover, and export for any platform.
The Common Mistake
When most people first try to generate video content, they type something like "a video of a cat." The result comes back generic: no movement direction, no tone, or structure.

feedbackCorrect.text: A vague prompt leaves every creative decision to Canva AI, and the result reflects that. Action, framing, and tone in the prompt are what turn a generic clip into something intentional.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Length and format aren't the issue. The Video tab needs direction, not more words. A short, specific prompt outperforms a long, vague one every time.

blocks.question: Why do you think a vague prompt like "a video of a cat" produces an unfocused result?

blocks.text: So the problem with "a video of a cat" is that it's a category, not a clear set of directions. Just like the Design tab, the more specific the input, the more usable the output. Let's see that in action.
Text to Video
The Video tab is a paid feature in Canva Pro that generates short clips based on a text prompt. Describe the subject, action, setting, and tone, and Canva AI builds the clip around those details.

Great, now if you want to change a detail, Canva AI's built-in settings let you go further. Style, Ratio, Audio, Framing, and Lighting can all be adjusted to make your prompt more structured and the output better.
Try it with a specific setup: a cartoon version. Select Cartoon style, Medium Shot framing, and Soft Lighting in the settings panel, and see what changes.

blocks.text: Here's how it looks with the same prompt, but with settings applied.

feedbackCorrect.text: Settings are creative decisions made before generation starts. Style, framing, and lighting tell Canva AI exactly how the clip should look — and the output reflects that precision.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Session order doesn't affect output quality, and a longer or more detailed prompt alone won't substitute for settings. The difference came from giving Canva AI specific visual direction through the settings panel — not from when it was generated or how the prompt was worded.

blocks.text: You've generated and customized your first clip. But there's still one thing we haven't tested — what happens when you make the prompt itself more specific. Let's find out.
Specific vs. Vague

The settings panel shapes the visual style, and the prompt itself controls what happens in the clip. Subject and action are a start, but setting and tone are what make the difference between a clip that could be anything and one that feels intentional.

blocks.prompt: Take the same subject and action, and add a setting and tone to see how the output changes.

blocks.text: You added the same subject — but with a setting and tone, the clip now has a specific mood and atmosphere.
Image to Video

A setting and tone in the prompt turned a generic clip into something with a specific mood and details. Now, take the process one step further and animate something that already exists as an image. Upload a photo or generate one in the Image tab first, and Canva AI turns it into a moving scene — the original image becomes the first frame, and the motion builds from there.

blocks.prompt: Generate an image to use as the base for your animation.

blocks.text: Now, once you have an image, let's upload it to the Video tab and animate it into a moving scene.

blocks.prompt: Take your generated image and animate it into a moving clip.

blocks.text: See how the still image turned into a moving scene with just a slow camera drift.
AI Voiceover

Canva AI doesn't stop at visuals; it can also bring your clip to life with a voice, too. Once your clip is ready, AI Voiceover assigns a synthesized voice to a typed script and syncs it to the video timeline in the Canva Editor. You can record a voiceover yourself or generate one with AI.
Type the script directly into the voiceover panel under Enter text, select the voice that fits the content, and Canva AI places the delivery against the clip.
Here's what you've got — an AI-made voiceover laid right over your clip, no recording needed.

You're not locked into one language either. Paste the translated version into the Enter text field, select your language, and Canva generates the voiceover in whichever language you choose. Let's try it in French with a female voice.
Here's how it sounds after switching to French.
Perfect!
You got all of that from one clip, one script, and one voiceover without ever leaving the editor. Here's the full workflow from start to finish:

1. Generate an image in the Image tab.
  2. Bring it into the Video tab.
  3. Animate it.
  4. Add a voiceover.
  5. Switch to another language.

• A specific prompt beats a vague one: Action, setting, and tone are what turn a generic clip into something intentional.
  • Image to Video connects the tabs: Generate an image first, then upload it and animate it directly in the Video tab.
  • AI Voiceover generates voice in multiple languages: Type a script, pick a language and voice, and Canva AI syncs it to your clip, no recording or rewriting required.

Every part of a generated element — questions, labels, colors, logic, and layout — can be adjusted through follow-up prompts. You can simply describe the changes in a prompt, and Canva AI updates the code behind it.
So, to make changes, just ask Canva AI to update the questions — for example:

You've created a quiz and made it personal just by describing what you wanted. That's the core idea behind the Code tab: it responds to plain language, whatever the project.

blocks.text: All of those problems come from building assets separately. This workflow keeps everything connected: one tab feeds the next, and the campaign stays consistent from the first image to the final interactive element. Let's build it.
Step 1: Create the Brand Logo
Before generating any campaign visuals, you need a logo that will anchor the brand across every asset. Let's create one in the Design tab — minimalistic, clean, and ready to use.

blocks.prompt: Generate a minimalistic logo for a brand called Lasyin in the Design tab.
blocks.template: Create [logo description] logo [style details] style for [brand segment] called [brand name]

blocks.text:
Look at the generated versions and pick the one that best matches the brand direction: clean, luxurious, and suited to a premium skincare product. 

That's your brand identity starting point. And to make sure it shows up consistently across every asset you generate from here, you need to lock it in.
Step 2: Set Up the Brand Kit

That's what the Brand Kit does. It locks in your logo, color palette, and brand voice, so every asset Canva AI generates reflects the same brand identity. Set it up once, and it applies across every tab and output that follows.
Step 3: Generate the Campaign Hero Image

With the Brand Kit set up, let's move on to the next step and create the hero image. Head to the Image tab and upload the logo. You can choose "Smart" as a style(it lets Canva select the most suitable visual style), 9:16 ratio (great for mobile and social platforms), and generate the product shot that will anchor the whole campaign.

blocks.text: Your hero image is ready, and the Brand Kit is locked in, meaning every asset from here will automatically carry the same logo and colors. Let's put that to work with the first campaign asset — a Facebook post.
Step 4: Build the Campaign Facebook Post

Head to the Design tab, upload the hero image as a reference, and let's generate the Facebook post. With the Brand Kit in place, the logo, colors, and typography will be applied automatically — no extra steps needed.

blocks.prompt: Use the Design tab to generate a Facebook post from your hero image with Brand Kit applied.
blocks.template: Create [asset type] for [platform]. Include the *uploaded image* in the post.

blocks.text: Excellent!

With the hero image and Facebook post ready, the visual side of the campaign is taking shape. 

But a strong marketing campaign doesn't stop at visuals — you need a copy that reaches your audience directly, too.
Step 5: Write the Campaign Email

An email is one of the most effective ways to reach your audience directly. Head to the Doc tab, select Email as the output type, add details on assets you've built, and ask Canva AI to write a launch email that introduces the Lasyin cream.

blocks.prompt: Generate tone-matched copy for your product launch campaign using the Doc tab.
blocks.template: Write [copy type] about [event]. Include a headline, caption, and product description. Tone: [description].

blocks.text:
Notice what happened: you specified "email" as the platform, and output arrived with a subject line, a structured body, and a length suited to how email gets read. 

If you change the platform to Instagram, the same brief comes back as a caption instead.
Perfect!
You've generated the hero image, the Facebook post, and the launch email. Now there's one more step: adding an interactive element that makes the campaign live.
Step 6: Build the Interactive Campaign Element

The Code tab handles that. Let's build a countdown timer for the Lasyin launch — once it's ready, embed it into your website or share it as a link alongside the post and email, so every part of the campaign works together.

blocks.prompt: Build an event countdown timer for your product launch using the Code tab.

blocks.text: The countdown can be embedded into your website, shared as a standalone link, or dropped into a presentation — whenever the launch date changes, just update the prompt and Canva AI rebuilds it instantly.

Now your campaign is complete: a logo, a hero image, a branded Facebook post, a launch email, and a live countdown, all ready to use. Before moving on, let's see how well you remember which tab handled what.

Canva AI for Sales

As a sales professional, you're constantly producing assets under time pressure — proposals, decks, follow-ups, and presentations that all need to look polished and land fast.

In this final lesson, Canva AI will help you optimize the process and turn a client brief into a complete proposal package in a single session.
The Sales Production Problem

Between writing proposals, chasing designers for decks, and formatting follow-up emails, a lot of selling time gets eaten up by production work. Each asset lives in a different tool at a different stage of the deal. 

Let's put the whole process in one place.

Imagine you just finished a client meeting with a chocolate brand — they need new packaging that better reflects the premium quality of their product. 

The deliverables: a proposal brief, a visual infographic, product visuals, and an ROI calculator. Let's build it step by step.
Step 1: Draft the Proposal on the Go

Proposal content doesn't have to wait until you're back at a desk. Create the client brief immediately after a meeting, and Canva AI generates the first draft of the deck structure and copy before the details fade. Let's handle this step first with the Doc tab.

blocks.template: Draft a proposal for [client] that needs [service]. Their issue: [problem]. Expected result: [outcome].
tokens: a cleaner, more luxurious visual identity

blocks.text: Great Work!
The brief is captured while the memory is still fresh. Next, let's turn it into something the client can actually look at.
Step 2: Build the Proposal Layout

A brief is a starting point, but it's not enough to send to a client. The client may need a branded proposal infographic, alongside the brief, to communicate the idea visually. Let's try building it by uploading the brief into the Design tab.

blocks.prompt: Use the Design tab to build a branded proposal layout for your client, with the brief uploaded as a reference.

blocks.text:
Notice that Canva generated the layout without knowing the brand name, so a few details will need manual updating before you send it.

Open Canva Editor to add the brand name — and while you're there, you can also refine the design, adjust colors, or swap out any images that don't quite fit.
Step 3: Generate Supporting Visuals
The brief and layout communicate the idea, but seeing the actual packaging makes it real. Let's add product visuals using the Image tab and show the client what the new packaging could look like.

blocks.prompt: Generate new packaging visuals for the chocolate proposal using the Image tab.

Now, the client can see the packaging you are producing, read the brief, and understand the offer. There's one thing left — something that moves a sales conversation from interesting to actionable: showing the client what the investment is actually worth.
Step 4: Build the Interactive Sales Tool
Let's add a real-life ROI calculator, let the client input their own figures, and see the projected return from the new packaging in real time with the Code tab — no developer needed.

Great Work!

As a sales professional, you now have everything you need to walk into any client conversation prepared — a structured brief, an infographic, product visuals, and a live calculator. The proposal package is ready to use now!

  • Build the layout in the Design tab: Upload the brief and generate a branded infographic that the client can actually look at.
  • Generate product visuals in the Image tab: Show what the new packaging will look like before it physically exists — adjust the style and ratio in the settings to match the context.
  • Make it interactive with the Code tab: Adding a functional element: calculator, quiz, or menu, turns a proposal into a decision-making tool the client uses.

blocks.text: Canva AI for Sales

As a sales professional, you're constantly producing assets under time pressure — proposals, decks, follow-ups, and presentations that all need to look polished and land fast.

In this final lesson, Canva AI will help you optimize the process and turn a client brief into a complete proposal package in a single session.
The Sales Production Problem

Between writing proposals, chasing designers for decks, and formatting follow-up emails, a lot of selling time gets eaten up by production work. Each asset lives in a different tool at a different stage of the deal. 

Let's put the whole process in one place.

Imagine you just finished a client meeting with a chocolate brand — they need new packaging that better reflects the premium quality of their product. 

The deliverables: a proposal brief, a visual infographic, product visuals, and an ROI calculator. Let's build it step by step.
Step 1: Draft the Proposal on the Go

Proposal content doesn't have to wait until you're back at a desk. Create the client brief immediately after a meeting, and Canva AI generates the first draft of the deck structure and copy before the details fade. Let's handle this step first with the Doc tab.

correctTokens: a cleaner, more luxurious visual identity
blocks.prompt: Ask Canva AI to draft a proposal brief for a chocolate brand's new packaging pitch.
blocks.template: Draft a proposal for [client] that needs [service]. Their issue: [problem]. Expected result: [outcome].
tokens: a cleaner, more luxurious visual identity

blocks.text: Great Work!
The brief is captured while the memory is still fresh. Next, let's turn it into something the client can actually look at.
Step 2: Build the Proposal Layout

A brief is a starting point, but it's not enough to send to a client. The client may need a branded proposal infographic, alongside the brief, to communicate the idea visually. Let's try building it by uploading the brief into the Design tab.

blocks.prompt: Use the Design tab to build a branded proposal layout for your client, with the brief uploaded as a reference.

blocks.text:
Notice that Canva generated the layout without knowing the brand name, so a few details will need manual updating before you send it.

Open Canva Editor to add the brand name — and while you're there, you can also refine the design, adjust colors, or swap out any images that don't quite fit.
Step 3: Generate Supporting Visuals
The brief and layout communicate the idea, but seeing the actual packaging makes it real. Let's add product visuals using the Image tab and show the client what the new packaging could look like.

blocks.prompt: Generate new packaging visuals for the chocolate proposal using the Image tab.

blocks.text: You can switch the style or aspect ratio in the settings if your task requires it. Let's see how choosing Macro style and a 3:4 Aspect Ratio changes the output.
Here's how the image changes when you apply different settings with the same prompt.
Perfect!

You can create visuals and change the output if you need, with settings.

Now, the client can see the packaging you are producing, read the brief, and understand the offer. There's one thing left — something that moves a sales conversation from interesting to actionable: showing the client what the investment is actually worth.
Step 4: Build the Interactive Sales Tool
Let's add a real-life ROI calculator, let the client input their own figures, and see the projected return from the new packaging in real time with the Code tab — no developer needed.

packaging investment and expected customer increase
blocks.prompt: Build an interactive ROI calculator for the chocolate packaging proposal using the Code tab.
blocks.template: Build [interactive tool] with inputs for [current metrics]. Show results for [what it calculates]. Keep the design in [colors].
tokens: current monthly customers and average order value
packaging investment and expected customer increase

blocks.text: Now you can share the calculator as a direct link alongside the proposal, embed it into your pitch deck, or send it as a standalone asset before the next call.
Great Work!

As a sales professional, you now have everything you need to walk into any client conversation prepared — a structured brief, an infographic, product visuals, and a live calculator. The proposal package is ready to use now!
